dabs Honestly, I'll try to put this into coherent words, my interpretation.

The anomaly was created by this GOI, and "implanted" into POI-17. POI-17, as a result, began to "lure" beings in by subconsciously subverting their natural instincts and freezing them, instilling safety into their mind, hence the starvation of the MTF's command, and the injuries of the MTF with no real sign of struggle (besides Vernon.)

Now, what I'm thinking is that, the reason why Vernon wasn't killed (from what I'm understanding) is that in some way, Vernon is the reason why the fetus exists (as in, he's the father somehow) and the fetus called out to him, because it knew it's fate in some way. Wanting to save his unborn son, he cuts it from POI-17 and leaves with it.

This is pre-reading the link at the end of the article. :P

item.content:encoded:
You flatter me so, I am happy to get such a glowing review of my works~! I didn't feel like I could post it as a mainlist skip and have it get as good of a reception as it has has. However, you can headcanon anything, you can even totally ignore mainlist skips. So I think that this tale can be "canonized" in the same way. And it's not an SCP, it's a URA, or Unregistered Anomaly. It's the designation given to anomalies that are recognized but not placed in the database yet in any way. Basically, this anomaly was being investigated and was in the process of becoming an SCP when this shit went down and it went off the radar.

and yes, ophite is one of my fav authors :3

EDIT: Though now the General Electric mention has been changed to a different company…

+1

When beginners write skips, I often tell them that they need a hook: an emotional connection, an interesting creepy effect, or a little mystery for the reader to solve. All of your works, author, seem to nail all three of those examples, and I think this piece is a really great example.

I do wish you had posted this as a mainlist skip, because I would like to see it "canonized," so to speak, and because I think it is an excellent example of an infohazards, and just how horrifying an infohazard can be.

(Also, was General Electric a reference to Ophites skips?)

item.content:encoded:
Unlike stuff like SCP-2710 (which has warmed on me over the years), which features back-and-forth discussion happening directly in the SCP document itself, your 001 proposal which is built around prose, or SCP-3999 where reality is breaking down both in the document itself and with the document itself reflecting reality breaking down, this tale just has the standard SCP stuff with corruption in it before it takes an immediate hard-right turn into actual prose. So for readers it can be very jarring for this to be a mainlist SCP. I list those three SCPs because I feel they are the closest to what this SCP represents in terms of style, but it doesn't really approach why any of those three SCPs work the way they work.

Now, granted, I actually would not be opposed to this being in the mainlist and I'd still upvote it, but I think it's just gonna be received better as a tale. 3999 would not work as a tale, your proposal would not work as a tale, 2710 would not work as a tale. This however is on the fence and can go either way, but it fits much better as a tale than an SCP on the whole.
